---- Respondents (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) For Petitioner : Mr. Parth Shrivastava, Advocate in both the petitions For State/Respondent No.1 : Mr. Malay Jain, Panel Lawyer For Respondent No.2 : Mr. Dharmesh Srivastava, Advocate in For Respondent No.2 : Mr.
Aniket Verma, Advocate in CRMP Hon'ble Shri Justice Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Hon'ble Shri Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad, J Order on Board Per Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice 05/12/2024 1.
Heard Mr. Parth Shrivastava, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner as well as Mr. Malay Jain, learned Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent.
Also heard Mr. Dharmesh Shrivastava, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 in CRMP No.513 of 2023 and Mr. Aniket Verma, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 in CRMP No. 3227 of 2024.

2. Both the petitions are arising out of FIR dated 06.11.2022 bearing Crime No.65/2022 registered before Police Station Mahila Thaha, Bilaspur, District - Bilaspur (C.G.), for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 294 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The CRMP No.513 of 2023 was filed by the in-laws of the complainant/respondent No.2 and CRMP.
No.3227 of 2024 was filed by the husband of the complainant/respondent No.2.
In both these petitions aforesaid FIR No.65/2022 was sought to be quashed and consequent thereof for quashment of entire proceedings against the petitioners.

3. The present petitions have been filed by the petitioners with the following prayer :
"It is, therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to set aside/quash the FIR dated 06.11.2022 (P/1) and the further proceeding initiated pursuant to Crime No.65/2022 registered before the Police Mahila Thana District,
Bilaspur of the alleged offence punishable under Section 498A, 294, 34 of IPC so far as it relates to the petitioner in the interest of justice"
4.

Facts of the case are that the petitioner in CRMP No. 3227 of 2024 and complaint/respondent No.2 got married on 20/04/2016 as per Hindu rituals and out of wedlock of their marriage they are Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13240312/
2 having two children.

entities.text: Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complainant alleges in her complaint that soon after the marriage the complainant's husband and in- laws started demanding dowry and started committing cruelty on her mentally and physically which made the present complaint.
She further states that earlier also she made a complaint on 19.06.2020 to Police station Mahila Thana, Bilaspur.
Wherein for once counseling was done and thereafter the husband and complainant both started living together and due to COVID-19 they both have not attended the counseling further.
It has been pointed out that the husband was having some affairs prior to their marriage.

The present complaint in crux is related to cruelty in connnection of demand of dowry due to which harrasment has been committed on complainant by the husband and her- in-laws during the period mentioned in the FIR which was registered on 06/11/2022 for offences under Sections 498-A, 294, 34 of IPC against the petitioners.

5. In CRMP No.513 of 2023, the petitioner No.01 is Father in law, petitioner No.02 is Grand Father in law, petitioners No.03 & 04 are two Brother in law and petitioner No.05 is Mother in law of the complainant/respondent No.2.

Likewise in CRMP No.3227 of 2024, the petitioner is the husband of the complainant/respondent No.2.
6.
Thereafter, the in-laws of the complainant/respondent No.2 have filed application for anticipatory bail before the concerned trial Court and the same was allowed vide order dated 16.11.2022.
The husband has also filed an application for anticipatory bail before this Court in which vide order dated 06.02.2023 passed in in MCRCA No.1680 of 2022 anticipatory bail was granted to him.
7. After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the jurisdictional Criminal Court.

8. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the complainant/respondent No.2 is wife of petitioner who has registered an FIR No.65 on 06.11.2022 against the petitioner and other co-accused persons who are in-laws for the offence under Section 498A, 294 read with 34 of IPC in which the charge-sheet has also been submitted against the petitioner and other co- accused persons.

9. Learned counsel appearing for the parties admitted that compromise has taken place between the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 in CRMP No.3227 of 2024 and they have settled their dispute amicably outside the Court, which has not been opposed by the counsel for the private respondent No.2, and as such, she does not want to continue with the criminal case and has compromised the case without any fear, undue influence or any pressure.
Therefore, the Criminal Case No.1662 of 2023 pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur be quashed.
10. The Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab & Another1 has laid down the following principles :

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab & Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"61. The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13240312/
3

entities.text: Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.

Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile,
civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding.
62. In view of the above, it cannot be said that B.S. Joshi, Nikhil Merchant and Manoj Sharma were not correctly decided.
We answer the reference accordingly.
Let these matters be now listed before the Bench(es) concerned."

11. The Supreme Court in B.S.Joshi & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Anr.1 has held as under :
"14.

entities.text: B.S.Joshi & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Anr.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no doubt that the object of introducing Chapter XX-A containing Section 498A in the Indian Penal Code was to prevent the torture to a woman by her husband or by relatives of her husband.
Section 498A was added with a view to punishing a husband and his relatives who harass or torture the wife to coerce her or her relatives to satisfy unlawful demands of dowry.

The hyper-technical view would be counter Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13240312/
4 productive and would act against interests of women and against the object for which this provision was added.

entities.text: Anup Kumar Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is every likelihood that non-exercise of inherent power to quash the proceedings to meet the 1 (2003) 4 SCC 675 ends of justice would prevent women from settling earlier.
That is not the object of Chapter XXA of Indian Penal Code.

15. In view of the above discussion, we hold that the High Court in exercise of its inherent powers can quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 of the Code."
12.

Furthermore, the Supreme Court in the case of Jitendra Raghuvanshi and others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and another 2 has examined scope of compromise under Section 320 of Cr.P.C. in offence of non-compoundable nature.

entities.text: Jitendra Raghuvanshi and others v. Babita Raghuvanshi and another 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. The Supreme Court referred to various cases and has laid down that in cases of matrimonial matters, court should exercise power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. sparingly and only it may exercise when the court is convinced, on the basis of material on record, that allowing the proceedings to continue would be an abuse of process of law or that the ends of justice require that the proceedings ought to be quashed.
14.

Considering the fact that as the dispute between petitioner and respondent No.2/wife of petitioner in CRMP No.3227 of 2024 is matrimonial in nature and the parties have entered in to compromise which is annexed as Annexure P/5.

The husband and wife are residing jointly along with their children and they are not having any dispute, which has been admitted by the counsel for the respondent No.2, who has filed memo of appearance in 2 (2013) 4 SCC 58 CRMP No.3227 of 2024.

Further the counsel for the respondent No.2 has given undertaking to withdraw her case arising out of the FIR No.65/2022 bearing Crime Case No.1662/2023 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur with her own, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the FIR No. 65/2022 and criminal proceedings of Criminal Case No.1662/2023 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur.

15. For the foregoing reasons, the both these petitions are allowed, the FIR No. 65/2022 and criminal proceedings of Criminal Case No.1662/2023 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 294 read with Section 34 of IPC against all the petitioners i.e. husband in CRMP No.3227 of 2024 and other co-accused persons who are the petitioner No.01 (Father in law), petitioner No.02 (Grand Father in law), petitioners No.03 &
04 (Brother in law) and petitioner No.05 (Mother in law) of the complainant/respondent No.2 in CRMP No.513 of 2024
are hereby quashed.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Amitendra Kishore Prasad) (Ramesh Sinha)
